summary: Gabbro is a Hearthian astronaut camped on an island on Giant's Deep, and the only Hearthian besides the Protagonist who remembers the 22-minute time loop. They play the flute and teach the Protagonist meditation, which can be used to end the current loop early.

behavior: Gabbro is friendly toward the Protagonist and displays a casual, laid-back attitude.
Gabbro is competent and clever regarding quantum mechanics and the time loop, despite their relaxed demeanor.
Gabbro responds to repeated death calmly and takes new experiences in stride.
Gabbro stares at cyclones long enough to be hypnotized into a trance.
Gabbro radios Hornfels about their experiences but Hornfels dismisses Gabbro's reports as confusion or dreams.
Gabbro pretends there is signal interference and tunes out when Hornfels talks too long.
Gabbro waits at their camp during the Eye of the Universe ending until the Protagonist gathers all other travelers.
Gabbro encourages the Protagonist to take time and not rush, both in-loop and during the final ending sequence.
location: Gabbro is located at their camp on Gabbro's Island on Giant's Deep.
Gabbro's spaceship is floating in the water near the cyclone around Giant's Deep's north pole.
Gabbro's camp has a campfire that the Protagonist can freely use to roast marshmallows.
Hornfels sent Gabbro to check the Deep Space Satellite at one point; Gabbro's log recording is found near the satellite.
lore: Gabbro is a member of Outer Wilds Ventures.
Gabbro is one of the Hearthian travelers.
Gabbro found multiple Nomai Statues on Giant's Deep.
Gabbro brought the first intact Nomai Statue from Statue Island to the Observatory on Timber Hearth.
Gabbro chipped the Nomai Statue while hauling it back to Timber Hearth; Slate later incorporated the chipped fragment into the ship's computer.
On the beach of Statue Island, Gabbro's Nomai Statue activated and glowed, replaying Gabbro's recent memories.
Gabbro paired with the Nomai Statue during the same loop as the Protagonist.
Gabbro and the Protagonist are the only beings aware of the time loop because they were the closest creatures to two Nomai Statues at the moment of pairing.
Gabbro started remembering loops at loop 9,318,054 — the same loop the Protagonist starts remembering.
Gabbro's theory: 'no glowing statue, no time loop awareness.'
Gabbro hypothesizes that perhaps only consciousnesses experience the loops, while bodies technically have not — because the loops never happen.
Gabbro told Spinel about being unable to reach the core of Giant's Deep during their first visit there.
Gabbro's flute sound is very airy and quietly pitched, making it hard to hear even with the Signalscope.
Gabbro's flute was made by Gneiss, as were all the Hearthian travelers' instruments.
Esker remarks that Gabbro never visits the Attlerock, saying simply 'Gabbro is Gabbro.'
Hal asks the Protagonist to say hi to Gabbro for them if they meet.
Hal hopes someone tells Gabbro or Riebeck that the Nomai Statue at the museum has opened its eyes.
Hornfels considers Gabbro 'our resident expert in leisurely whiling away the hours.'
Hornfels recorded Gabbro's '3 Foolproof Steps for Dozing Off' in notes near the Radio Tower.
Hornfels remarks that Gabbro deliberately burns their marshmallows.
Gabbro wrote a quantum poem in the Quantum Grove on Timber Hearth that works out to be 24 poems when read in different observation orders.
Gabbro plans to make more quantum art, including a creature sculpture that appears and startles observers.
The Museum Shard placard mentions Gabbro's theory that the shard 'exists in all possible states until it is observed.'
Most Hearthians dismiss Gabbro's quantum theory about the Museum Shard as an optical illusion, though they agree it is creepy.
Gabbro found nothing wrong with the Deep Space Satellite when Hornfels sent them to investigate.
Gabbro nicknames the Deep Space Satellite 'Ol' Spacey.'
Gabbro told the Deep Space Satellite that it was doing a great job during their inspection.
Gabbro mused that they would not mind floating endlessly and napping in the velvety darkness among the stars.
The radio tower on Timber Hearth contains a photo of Gabbro from when Hornfels sent them to check the Deep Space Satellite.
If asked about the Orbital Probe Cannon's destruction by excess power, Gabbro notes it sounds like something Slate or Feldspar would do.
Gabbro considers it 'wild' upon learning that the Nomai built the time loop device inside Ash Twin's core.
mechanics: Selecting Gabbro's 'How do you stay so calm in the face of repeated impending death?' dialogue option teaches the Protagonist how to meditate.
The meditation dialogue option is unlocked on the third loop and requires having spoken to Gabbro in a prior loop.
Meditating ends the current loop early and adds the meditation option to the pause menu.
Gabbro's first-loop dialogue is unique because they have not yet experienced death.
Gabbro's second-loop dialogue is unique because they have radioed Hornfels about dying.
On the third loop and later, Gabbro recognizes the time loop and discusses theories with the Protagonist.
Gabbro hints at Statue Island as a place to explore: it is the island with two pieces connected by a natural rock arch.
Gabbro warns that if a cyclone picks up the player on Giant's Deep, landing in water is less likely to kill them than landing on land.
Gabbro mentions that a strong current beneath Giant's Deep's surface prevents anything from sinking below it, and they could not find a way past it.
Gabbro mentions seeing a bright flash in the sky at the start of every loop, hinting at the Orbital Probe Cannon's destruction in orbit.
